c.tagline: A vertical cascade of pastel houses tumbling down to the sea, the postcard image of the Amalfi Coast

card: Widely accepted; cash useful for small boutiques and beach clubs

taxi.fare: Metered, but often high fixed rates given the steep, narrow roads
taxi.fareNote: Taxis are expensive and roads are notoriously congested in peak season; the SITA bus or a boat is often more practical

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU-style emergency number that connects to police, fire, and ambulance

english.label: Easy to get by in English

walk: Positano is famously vertical, with steep stairs connecting the upper town to the beach; comfortable shoes are essential, and a local shuttle bus helps with the steepest sections

safety.safety: Very safe town, though extremely crowded and expensive in peak summer
safety.crime: Petty theft in crowded areas during peak season is the main concern

hood_landmark.Marina Grande: Marina Grande beach and Santa Maria Assunta's majolica dome
hood_landmark.Montepertuso: Montepertuso's hilltop village and natural rock arch
hood_landmark.Nocelle: Nocelle's clifftop hamlet at the start of the Path of the Gods
hood_landmark.Via Cristoforo Colombo (Upper Town): The upper town's boutique-lined main road

avoid.reason: Pickpockets work the crowded SITA buses and ferry queues in summer; keep bags zipped in the crush.

hood_desc: The main beach and harbor at the base of town, with the iconic church dome and most restaurants and boat departures.
A short walk (or water taxi) from Marina Grande, a calmer pebble beach popular with locals.
A hilltop village above Positano reached by local bus, with sweeping views and a famous natural rock arch.
An even higher, quieter hamlet at the trailhead for the Path of the Gods hike, offering dramatic coastal panoramas.
The steep main street winding down from the top of town, lined with boutiques, ceramics shops, and cafes.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, though many visitors buy bottled for taste.

transit.sys: SITA regional buses and a local shuttle bus within Positano; seasonal boats along the coast
transit.pay: Tickets purchased at tabacchi shops before boarding
transit.note: The SITA bus along the Amalfi Coast road is scenic but slow and crowded; boats are often faster between coastal towns

transport.air: Naples International Airport (NAP), about 1.5-2 hr away by road
transport.train: Nearest train station is Salerno or Sorrento, followed by bus or boat to Positano
transport.bus: SITA buses connect Positano to Sorrento, Amalfi, and Salerno along the coast road
transport.ferry: Seasonal ferries connect Positano to Sorrento, Amalfi, Capri, and Naples
transport.car: Notoriously narrow, congested coastal roads in peak season; many visitors prefer the boat or bus

airport.name: Naples International Airport
airport.transport: Private transfer, bus via Sorrento, or rental car

net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: A TIM, Vodafone, or WindTre tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: Not obligatory; rounding up is appreciated for guides and tours
tip.r: A cover charge (coperto) is common instead of tipping; rounding up is a nice gesture

food.name: Spaghetti alle vongole
food.desc: Spaghetti tossed with vongole veraci, olive oil, garlic, white wine and parsley. The dish every Positano beach kitchen is judged on.

places.name: Chez Black
places.note: Beachfront institution since 1949, widely rated for the best vongole in town.

places.name: Da Vincenzo
places.note: Family-run since 1958; a locals' benchmark for seafood pasta done simply.

places.name: Buca di Bacco
places.note: Historic hotel restaurant on the beach promenade, strong on classic clam pasta.

food.name: Totani e patate
food.desc: Positano's own dish: local squid stewed slowly with potatoes, tomato and herbs until soft. Rarely found outside this stretch of coast.

places.name: Da Vincenzo
places.note: Keeps the traditional Positanese recipe on the menu year-round.

places.name: Il Ritrovo
places.note: Hillside village kitchen known for old Positano recipes and its own garden produce.

places.name: Lo Guarracino
places.note: Terrace on the cliff path, long-standing address for home-style coast cooking.

food.name: Scialatielli ai frutti di mare
food.desc: Short, thick Amalfi Coast egg pasta with mussels, clams, prawns and cherry tomatoes. Invented on this coastline in the 1960s.

places.name: Lo Guarracino
places.note: Sea-view pergola and a reliable seafood pasta list at fair Positano prices.

places.name: Da Vincenzo
places.note: House-made pasta and daily market seafood; book ahead in summer.

places.name: Il Ritrovo
places.note: Free shuttle from Positano centre up to the village; generous seafood plates.

food.name: Frittura di paranza
food.desc: Basket of tiny whole fish, squid and prawns flash-fried in light batter and eaten with lemon and your fingers, right by the water.

places.name: Da Adolfo
places.note: Reached by the free wooden boat from Positano jetty; barefoot beach-shack classic.

places.name: Chez Black
places.note: Beach terrace fry-ups paired with a chilled coast white at sunset.

places.name: Lo Guarracino
places.note: Quieter cliffside spot for fried seafood away from the beach crowds.

food.name: Pesce all'acqua pazza
food.desc: Whole sea bass or bream poached in crazy water of tomato, garlic, olive oil and sea water, then filleted at the table.

places.name: La Sponda
places.note: Positano's Michelin-starred room, candlelit terrace; the refined version of the dish.

places.name: Da Adolfo
places.note: Simple grilled and poached whole fish straight off the boats.

places.name: Buca di Bacco
places.note: Fish counter by the entrance so you pick your own before it is cooked.

food.name: Delizia al limone
food.desc: Dome of lemon-soaked sponge filled and coated with lemon cream, made with sfusato lemons from the terraces above town.

places.name: La Zagara
places.note: Historic pasticceria and garden cafe; the town's most photographed lemon cakes.

places.name: Casa e Bottega
places.note: Bright all-day cafe with lighter, freshly baked lemon desserts and juices.

places.name: Buca di Bacco
places.note: Reliable end-of-meal delizia on the beachfront terrace.

food.name: Limoncello
food.desc: Icy digestivo made by steeping thick-skinned Amalfi sfusato lemon peel in alcohol. Poured free at the end of most Positano meals.

places.name: La Zagara
places.note: Makes its own limoncello and sells bottles alongside the pastries.

places.name: Chez Black
places.note: Sunset limoncello at the sand-side tables is a Positano ritual.

places.name: Da Vincenzo
places.note: House limoncello and lemon granita to close the meal.

food.name: Costa d'Amalfi white wine
food.desc: Crisp Falanghina, Biancolella and Furore Bianco grown on the coast's vertical terraces. The natural match for clams and fried fish.

places.name: Franco's Bar
places.note: Cliff-edge aperitivo bar with coast wines and the best sunset view in Positano.

places.name: Buca di Bacco
places.note: Deep Campania wine list in a hotel that has poured here for generations.

places.name: Da Vincenzo
places.note: Small wine bar beside the restaurant for by-the-glass local bottles.

landmarks: Spiaggia Grande
Positano's main beach spreads beneath the famous pastel cascade of cliffside houses, backed by bobbing yachts and chic beach clubs.
Church of Santa Maria Assunta
Its majolica-tiled dome glitters above the beach, while inside a Byzantine Black Madonna icon anchors the legend of Positano's founding.
Sentiero degli Dei (Path of the Gods)
The Amalfi Coast's legendary clifftop trail from Bomerano to Nocelle dangles walkers five hundred meters above the bluest sea in Italy.
Via dei Mulini
Positano's bougainvillea-draped main lane winds down to the sea past lemon-granita stands, sandal makers and the boutiques that invented Moda Positano.
Fornillo Beach
A cliff-hugging footpath past medieval watchtowers leads to this quieter grey-pebble cove, favored by locals and its laid-back beach bars.
Li Galli Islands
The sirens of Greek myth supposedly sang from this private offshore archipelago, once owned by Rudolf Nureyev and best admired by boat.
MAR Positano (Roman Archaeological Museum)
Beneath the church crypt lies a Roman villa buried by Vesuvius in 79 AD, its vividly colored frescoes astonishingly preserved underground.
Montepertuso
This cliff village above Positano is named for the hole pierced through its mountain, allegedly punched by the Madonna while defeating the devil.
Nocelle
A near-carless hamlet at the end of the Path of the Gods, its tiny terraces serve fresh lemon granita with vertiginous coastline views.
Arienzo Beach
Reached by some three hundred steps, this cliff-framed cove catches sunshine late into the afternoon, with a stylish beach club and fewer crowds.

train.note: Positano has no railway - the Amalfi Coast was never given a line. The nearest stations are Salerno, about 90 minutes east by bus or ferry, and Sorrento on the Circumvesuviana narrow-gauge line from Naples (https://www.eavsrl.it/), roughly 50 minutes away by bus. Trenitalia (https://www.trenitalia.com) services for the rest of Italy start from Salerno or Naples.

bus.note: No international coaches. SITA Sud (https://www.sitasudtrasporti.it/) buses grind along the coast road between Sorrento, Positano, Amalfi and Salerno - beautiful but slow and extremely crowded in summer, when the road can gridlock. Buy tickets before boarding at a tabacchi. The internal Mobility Amalfi Coast orange buses shuttle up and down Positano's steep lanes.

intl.to: Amalfi, Salerno, Sorrento & Capri (Italy) - seasonal fast ferry, Apr-Oct

ferry.note: In season the ferry is by far the best way in and out of Positano - it takes about 40 minutes to Amalfi and 70 to Salerno, skipping the coast road entirely, and the approach from the water is the classic view of the town. Boats leave from the Spiaggia Grande jetty. Services run roughly April to October, are cancelled in rough seas, and stop altogether over winter, when the bus is the only option.

half.name: Capri
half.blurb: Island reached by ferry in under an hour holds the Blue Grotto sea cave and cliffside gardens above the Faraglioni rock stacks.

half.name: Amalfi
half.blurb: Coastal town about 25 minutes away by boat or bus centers on a striped medieval cathedral and a former maritime republic's harbor.

half.name: Ravello
half.blurb: Clifftop town about 45 minutes away holds the terraced gardens of Villa Cimbrone and Villa Rufolo, overlooking the coast above Amalfi.

half.name: Pompeii
half.blurb: Buried Roman city about 90 minutes away by bus and train preserves streets, houses and plaster casts frozen by the 79 AD eruption.

half.name: Mount Vesuvius
half.blurb: Active volcano above the Bay of Naples, about two hours away, has a crater rim trail reached after a steep gravel climb.
